div.head: Ine 71
div.ab: CXV. Gif mon sie wertyhtlan betogen ⁊ he hit þonne geondette beforan aðe ⁊ onsace ǽr, bide mon mid þære witerædenne, oð ðæt se wer gegolden sie.
CXV. Gif mon sy wertyhtlan betogen ⁊ he hit þonne geondette beforan aþe ⁊ onsace ær, abide man mid ðære witerædene, oð þæt se wer gegolden sy.
Be wertyhlan. Gyf mon sy wertyhlan betogen ⁊ he hit ðonne geandette beforan aðe ⁊ onsace ær, abide mon mid ðære witerædenne, oð þæt se wer gegolden sy.
Si homo (quis) sit de homicidio accusatus et idem confiteatur ante iusiurandum et prius abnegasset, expectetur de wite redditione, donec ipsa wera reddita sit.
[Be wertyhlan.] Gif mon sie wertyhtlan betogen ⁊ he hit þonne geondette beforan aðe ⁊ onsace ǽr, bide mon mid þære witerædenne, oð ðæt se wer gegolden sie.
{CXV} Gif mon sie wertyhtlan betogen ⁊ he hit þonne geondette beforan aðe ⁊ onsace ǽr, bide mon mid þære witerædenne, oð ðæt se wer gegolden sie.

Wenn jemand in Klage auf Wergeld verklagt wird und er es nun vor dem [zu leistenden Reinigungs]eide eingesteht, obwohl er [es] vorher geleugnet [hatte], so warte man mit dem Strafgeld-Erheben, bis dass das Wergeld [des Erschlagenen vom Todtschläger an dessen Sippe] bezahlt ist.

If someone is accused in a claim for wergeld and he now confesses it before the [exculpatory] oath [is to be sworn], although he had previously denied [it], let the levying of the fine wait until the wergeld [of the slain man has been paid by the killer to his kin].

If a man is accused on a charge involving the payment of wergeld, and [if], when he is required to give an oath, he confesses the act, which he has previously denied, no proceedings shall be taken to secure the fine until the wergeld has been paid.
If anyone is accused on a charge involving payment of wergild, and he then admits it before the oath, and has previously denied it, one is to wait for the fine until the wergild has been paid.
If a person is accused of an act for which wergild must be paid and then confesses on oath but has denied it previously, one should wait to collect the fine until the wer has been paid.

Nicht ‘um ein mit seinem Wergeld strafbares Verbrechen’ (Price; s. o. 54), sondern durch Sippe des Erschlagenen wegen eines Totschlags; denn Wergeld tritt hier in Ggs. zum Strafgeld. Der bisher unbeeidete Leugner zieht dem ihm durch Beweisurteil zuerkannten Reinigungseide die Wergeldzahlung vor; vgl. Gl Priorität 3; Geständnis 1

Not ‘for a crime punishable by his wergild’ (Price; see above 54), but [accused] by the kindred of the slain man on account of a homicide; for wergild here stands in contrast to the fine. The denier, not yet on oath, prefers paying the wergild to the oath of exculpation awarded to him by the judgment on proof; cf. Gl Priorität 3; Geständnis 1

Für Totschlag (s. d. Gl 7) erhält der Richter Fechtstrafe, daneben für Wortbruch (Brunner II 368 f. 621): si quis negaverit . ., et super hoc iuramentum prestare noluerit, sed pocius reddere quam iurare maluerit, eo quod prius negavit, persolvet; aus Stadtrecht Ripen a. 1269 c. 46 zitiert von Price

For homicide (see that word in Gl 7) the judge receives the fighting-fine, and in addition [a fine] for breach of word (Brunner II 368 f. 621): si quis negaverit . ., et super hoc iuramentum prestare noluerit, sed pocius reddere quam iurare maluerit, eo quod prius negavit, persolvet; from the town law of Ripen a. 1269 c. 46, cited by Price

It is not clear whether the reference is to homicide, in which case the wergeld would be that of the man slain, or to some serious crime which involved the payment of the perpetrator’s own wergeld (see note 1 to cap. 72, below). Liebermann takes the former view; but it is possible to take this law in connection with cap. 72, which would mean the payment of the perpetrator’s own wergeld.
